title: One partition answers one question; an inverted index answers the reverse
captions: Member m1 has three items under one partition key. Together they are an item collection. The sort key keeps them in order: CLUB# items, then PROFILE.
Access pattern: "show this member's clubs". One Query with the partition key and a sort key prefix returns both clubs. The club name was copied in, so no second read is needed.
Add a second member. Now ask the reverse question: "who is in club c1?". CLUB#c1 sits in the sort key of many partitions. The table cannot find them without reading everything.
A global secondary index (GSI) with the keys swapped fixes this. Only membership items carry its keys, so profiles stay out. All of c1's members land in one index partition.
The cost: DynamoDB updates the index asynchronously, usually within a fraction of a second. A query on it can miss a member who joined a moment ago.
